InteractionAudioFidelityContract.v1.scope: all OpenRemaster game projects and ReconstructionAdapters
InteractionAudioFidelityContract.v1.unit: interaction branch / trigger / puzzle transition / NPC-dialog activation / automatic gameplay side-effect
rules: Every reconstructed interaction unit MUST have an explicit audio classification.
Audio MUST NOT be inferred from semantic category alone; generic pickup/use/door/dialog sounds are forbidden unless source-backed.
NPC/dialog voice MUST NOT be synthesized or inferred from text when canonical voice evidence is absent.
Successful and failed branches are classified independently; audio from a successful branch MUST NOT leak into a silent failure branch.
SOURCE_AUDIO_VERIFIED requires provenance to corpus/oracle evidence, asset identity when applicable, runtime event binding, and validation.
NO_AUDIO_BY_SOURCE requires evidence that the reconstructed branch is intentionally silent; silence is a fidelity result, not missing implementation.
HOLD_UNRESOLVED forbids guessing and blocks FIDELITY_VERIFIED promotion when the unresolved audio could materially affect the slice.
Canonical source assets MUST retain hashes/provenance; substitutions require explicit non-fidelity labeling.
Logical audio events and physical playback MUST share the same canonical binding so replay, diagnostics and packaged runtime cannot diverge.
The interaction-audio matrix MUST expand with reconstructed scope; structural completeness cannot silently omit audio semantics.
InteractionAudioFidelityContract.v1.adapter_responsibility: Game/engine adapter maps canonical AudioEventIR bindings to runtime playback; framework contract does not prescribe WAV, Miles, MIDI, Redbook, streamed voice, or engine-specific formats.
